claims.text: An active-learning machine-learning potential can improve representation of ab initio liquid configurations in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Improved representation by the active-learning MLP will enhance reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved representation by the active-learning MLP will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The proposed method is applicable to alloys containing three to six principal elements.
The proposed method is applicable from 0.8 to 1.2 times the alloy melting temperature.
The MLP can learn the complex potential-energy surface of high-entropy alloys from ab initio data.
Learning from ab initio data reduces reliance on EAM references to represent relevant atomic configurations.
The proposed MLP will provide better reference–target phase-space overlap than TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed MLP will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed method is expected to predict the solid–liquid transition temperature within 50 K of experiment.
A transition-temperature deviation greater than 50 K from experiment would falsify the hypothesis.
